name: Brick wall alignment (plumb/level check)

steps.title: Safety gear and stable footing
steps.visual_criteria: Safety boots and gloves worn; clean working platform clear of loose rubble

steps.title: Mortar bed consistency and spreading
steps.visual_criteria: Mortar bed spread 10-12mm thick uniformly across brick course with trowel groove

steps.title: Brick placement and bond overlap
steps.visual_criteria: Bricks laid with frog up, half-brick staggered overlap (stretcher bond) maintained

steps.title: Plumb bob vertical check
steps.visual_criteria: Plumb bob suspended from top course hanging 1-2mm clear of face without touching or leaning

steps.title: Spirit level horizontal alignment
steps.visual_criteria: Spirit level placed across brick course shows bubble centered between reference lines

scenario_questions.text: How do you verify that a newly laid brick course is perfectly horizontal and vertical?
expected_points: Use a spirit level for horizontal level across top course
Use a plumb rule or plumb bob for vertical straightness

scenario_questions.text: Why must bricks be wetted before laying them with cement mortar?
expected_points: Prevents dry bricks from absorbing water from the wet mortar
Ensures proper hydration and bonding strength of cement

scenario_questions.text: What maximum height of brick wall should you construct in a single day?
expected_points: Not more than 1.5 meters (about 5 feet) per day
Allows mortar to set and avoids wall tilting under self-weight

common_mistakes: Not checking vertical alignment with plumb bob every 2-3 courses
Using dry bricks that draw moisture from mortar
Laying continuous vertical joints without proper overlap
